verbatim_verdict_text:
## Observations in order

1. **0.0–1.4 s — WEBSITE loading surface:**  
   The frame is almost entirely blank, with a gray band along the bottom. This is loading chrome rather than identifiable extension work.

2. **1.4–4.0 s — WEBSITE navigation:**  
   The D&D Beyond header and logo appear, followed by navigation links, search, sign-in, and **CREATE ACCOUNT**. These are the website’s own surfaces.

3. **4.0–6.8 s — WEBSITE loading and privacy dialog:**  
   A D&D Beyond loading card and spinner appear. The site then displays its own **“Your Privacy Choices”** panel with “Cookie Settings,” “Accept All,” and “Reject Non-Essential Cookies.” The cookie panel and buttons are website work, not extension work.

4. **6.2–29.2 s — WEBSITE character sheet with EXTENSION enhancement:**  
   The character sheet for **Corvo Saggio** loads. Its artwork, portrait, abilities, skills, actions, inventory, hit points, and other sheet content are website work. Over those website elements, thin red rounded outlines and drag-related styling appear. These enhanced borders/guides are attributable to the extension, although they do not use the described dark-and-gold “codex” treatment. The privacy panel is dismissed around 7.8 s, but that dismissal itself is not clearly shown.

5. **29.2–30.2 s — EXTENSION-enhanced sheet viewport:**  
   The view shifts downward and crops the sheet into a mostly whitespace-heavy layout. Red outlines still identify extension-managed elements. No extension control panel is yet visible in this cropped view.

6. **30.2–33.6 s — EXTENSION control panel and LAYER MANAGEMENT panel:**  
   Two clearly extension-authored dark panels appear:
   - Left: a floating panel with **LAYOUT** and **OUTPUT**, including Load, Reset to Default, Manage Clones, Add Shape, Manage Compact, AI Arrange, AI Settings, Print, Print Settings, and Save to Browser.
   - Right: **LAYER MANAGEMENT**, listing **SECTIONS (22)** and **SHAPES (1)**, with section and shape entries.
   
   An extension toast states **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”** A separate **“Shapes (Default) loaded”** status also appears. The layer manager shows several shape thumbnails, including labels such as “Archer Accent A,” “Archer Accent B,” and “Archer Divider.”

7. **33.2–33.8 s — EXTENSION template/status behavior:**  
   The sheet visibly changes to an ornate decorative template, accompanied by **“Shapes (Default) loaded.”** This is an extension-driven template/shape rendering.

8. **33.8–end — EXTENSION shape picker:**  
   A centered dark **“SELECT DECORATIVE SHAPE”** dialog opens with BORDERS, SHAPES, and CUSTOM tabs, category filters, a search field, and an ARCHER group containing three visible thumbnail previews. The thumbnails render on camera. **Add Shape** is visibly disabled because no item appears selected. The video ends with the picker still open, so no shape is actually added.

## Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Assertion | Result | On-camera basis |
|---|---|---|
| A shape added from the picker renders from a `.webp` asset | **NOT-VISIBLE** | The picker opens and its previews render, but the test never selects or adds a shape before the video ends. No added shape is shown, and the asset format cannot be established visually. |
| Picker previews load from `.webp` assets, with no `.gif` references | **NOT-VISIBLE** | Three picker previews visibly load, but camera frames cannot reveal whether their URL or MIME type is `.webp`; no `.gif` reference is shown either, so the contract is not demonstrated. |
| Layer Manager shape thumbnails point to `.webp` assets that load | **NOT-VISIBLE** | Shape thumbnails are visibly present in the Layer Manager and appear loaded, but their backing asset paths cannot be confirmed as `.webp` from the recording. |

## Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

### Extension UI distinguishability
The extension is clearly distinguishable from the base website when its panels appear: both the floating control panel and Layer Management use dark workbench-style surfaces, while the D&D Beyond page remains white/red. The shape picker is likewise clearly extension-authored and visually distinct.

The sheet enhancement itself is less distinctive: the visible extension treatment is mainly thin red rounded outlines around otherwise ordinary D&D Beyond sections. No clearly visible gold hairlines, dark codex styling, drag grips, or alignment guides appear in the sampled enhanced-sheet views.

### Basic affordances observed working
- The extension’s floating panel opens and exposes LAYOUT and OUTPUT sections.
- Layer Management opens and visibly lists sections and shapes.
- A “no saved layout yet” informational toast appears.
- A “Shapes (Default) loaded” status/toast appears.
- A decorative template/shape rendering appears on the sheet after the loaded status.
- The shape picker opens with tabs, category filters, a search field, and a searchable asset group.
- Three shape preview images visibly load.
- The **Add Shape** button has a clear disabled state while no picker item is selected.
- The **Cancel** button is visibly available for dismissing the picker.

### Basic affordances observed missing or rough
- The requested shape-add completion is missing: the recording ends with the picker open and **Add Shape** disabled.
- No applied shape is shown after selection, so the add flow, success toast, and resulting page rendering are not demonstrated.
- No undo flow is visible.
- No error state is visible.
- No extension loading or transition animation is clearly shown.
- No toolbar icon or visible **ON badge** is shown.
- No explicit activation transition from the plain sheet to the enhanced sheet is captured; the enhancement simply appears as the page loads.
- The “Shapes (Default) loaded” message appears while the visible sheet changes to a different ornate template, making the status wording somewhat ambiguous.
- The sheet enhancement is visually subtle and primarily red-on-white, unlike the extension panels’ dark-and-gold workbench styling.
- The picker’s underlying layer-manager shape previews are small, making asset rendering difficult to inspect.
- Although a hover tooltip says **“Drag to move”** and **“Drag corners to resize”**, no actual dragging or resizing interaction is visibly exercised.

Because the video records substantial extension UI and visible image rendering, this is not a blank or too-few-frame recording. However, none of the format-specific WebP assertions can be established from camera evidence, and the principal shape-add interaction is left unfinished.

VERDICT: NOT-VISIBLE
